The 4 levels of using AI at work How to use AI at work: there are four levels, and most people never leave level one. Chat. You paste something into ChatGPT or Claude, it answers, you copy it back out. Useful, but you're the delivery guy carrying every answer between your apps by hand. Context. Give it your price list, your process docs and ten emails you wrote so it learns how you sound. Same AI, completely different answers, because now it answers like it works at your company. Connected tools. Out of the box, AI can't open your CRM or read your spreadsheet. Almost every app has a door for other software called an API, and MCP is a standard plug that lets AI walk through those doors. Once it's connected, it sees your contacts, your sheets and your email, and it acts: update, send, create. Updating 2,000 customer records from last month's invoices is two weeks of somebody's life. Connected AI does it in minutes. Run it on ten records first, check them, then let it do the rest. Automations. Level three still needs you to ask. Level four starts on its own: a new lead comes in, an invoice lands, Monday at 8am. A tool like n8n moves the data between your apps, and the AI in the middle does the thinking: reads the email, picks the category, writes the reply. Your business keeps running while you sleep. The whole ladder: chat, context, connected tools, automations. On level three you talk and it does the work. On level four you don't even have to talk. If you want to climb all four, from your first chat to your first AI automation, I built seven courses for exactly that, in order, inside my community. The 6 levels of AI (and why you can't skip one) Most people think they're good at AI because they use it every day. That's level one. There are six. You don't use it. You tried it once, got something generic, and decided it's overhyped. Chat. Ask, get an answer, copy it somewhere. It saves minutes, but every chat starts from zero. Context. Write one page about your work: who you are, your customers, how you write, what good looks like. Stop rewriting the prompt. Projects and skills. The page lives in a project with your files. Your repeatable jobs become skills, so the AI follows your steps the same way every time. Automations. A new lead gets a drafted reply before you open your laptop. A late invoice gets a reminder on day three. You stop being the trigger. Agents. Give it a goal, not steps. It plans, uses your tools, checks its own work, and asks you before anything important. A team of AI employees. Each one has a lane, its own instructions, tools and memory. They hand work to each other and tell you what needs you. The part that matters: every level sits on the one under it. Context makes skills work. Skills make automations reliable. Reliable automations are what agents use. Find your level honestly, then do the next one. Not the top one. Inside my community I have every level, in order, in eight courses, from your first chat to a team of AI employees.
